text:
anna: heads-up — after the RBAC rewrite merged last night, on-prem admin users for customer 'acme-onprem-42' cannot reach the private control plane. repro below, blocking support call.

ryan: can you paste the minimal repro + any logs? which cluster/env?

anna: repro (quick):
1) clone customer env access
2) attempt to open admin console /api/v1/admin/info
3) get 403 from control plane and KMS denies for token unwrap

logs:
```
2026-03-18T21:12:05Z controlplane auth ERROR "request denied" user=onprem-admin@acme reason=AccessDenied KMS=projects/redwood/keys/private-01 action=Decrypt
2026-03-18T21:12:05Z kube-audit WARN "subjectaccessreview failed" user=system:serviceaccount:onprem:controlplane-svc account=onprem-admin
```

claire: FYI PR #4321 (rbac: refactor role mappings) landed 03:12 UTC; it changed the onprem-admin clusterrole -> replaced broad composite role with smaller capability set.

sanjay: is this only private/on-prem or also affecting Dedicated?

anna: only private control plane (on-prem). Dedicated customers unaffected. probably because dedicated uses an older role mapping path.

devops-bot: deploy status: rollout rbac-refactor v2 -> 100% complete on prod-onprem-clusters (timestamp 1743217500) :information_source:

claire: quick mitigation: we can temporarily rebind the previous composite role for the affected customer while we fix the policy. e.g. run:
```bash
kubectl create clusterrolebinding acme-onprem-admin-binding --clusterrole=redwood:onprem-admin-full --user=onprem-admin@acme
```

anna: tried that, control plane responds 200 now for admin endpoints, but KMS still logs AccessDenied on wrap/unwrap. seems RBAC fix surfaced a KMS principal change.

sanjay: paste the KMS policy from the key used by that env (mask ARNs).

anna: KMS policy snippet from key policy (redacted):
```
"Principal": {"AWS": ["arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/redwood-onprem-role-old"]},
"Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:Encrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey"],
"Effect": "Allow"
```

sanjay: ah — RBAC rewrite changed the principal the control plane uses to assume the role (now uses role/redwood-onprem-role-new). key policy still only allows the old role. that explains the KMS denies.

claire: two paths: 1) update key policy to add new role (needs compliance signoff), or 2) revert the principal mapping to old role while we finish the key policy change. which is faster for support?

anna: for the customer call in 30m, revert mapping to old role in the control plane for that tenant. we can schedule key policy change after approval.

irene: tagging compliance: we need an audit record for any KMS key policy change. If you update the key policy, include justification, affected tenants, and timeframe.

claire: I'll trigger a targeted revert for acme-onprem-42 and open a change request for KMS policy update. running rollback now (canary).

deploy-bot: Rollback triggered: rbac-refactor v2 -> revert mapping for tenant=acme-onprem-42 by claire (ts=1743220300) :rocket:

anna: confirm after rollback — admin access restored and KMS decrypts succeed now. verifying logs...

anna: verification logs:
```
2026-03-18T21:34:12Z controlplane auth INFO "request allowed" user=onprem-admin@acme action=admin:read
2026-03-18T21:34:12Z kms INFO "Decrypt OK" key=private-01 principal=arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/redwood-onprem-role-old
```

sanjay: we'll schedule a proper key-policy update and a config rollout to make new role explicit, with compliance review. recording action items.

irene: please file an incident with severity P2: include timeline, PR id, tenant list, and KMS change request link. I'll own the audit entries.

anna: filing incident now and adding logs + repro. thanks all. :thumbsup:

claire: follow-up: add regression test to CI that validates KMS principal permissions for on-prem role mappings before merge. PR incoming. :eyes:
